description:
Poll a 2FA session until the user completes the challenge. Uses exponential backoff (2s initial, 1.5x, 30s max) with jitter.

Agent usage: Call this after start_2fa with the returned session_id. Terminal states: "verified" (challenge completed — proceed with the protected operation), "expired" (offer to restart with start_2fa). Before polling, present start_2fa's challenge: pass its `deep_link` to render_auth_link on telegram/whatsapp, or show its `sms_message` on sms.

The user does not see tool results — most clients fold them away, render_auth_link's output included. Before you wait or poll, put what the user must act on into your own reply text: the link itself (not a sentence announcing it), the SMS text and number, or a note to check their inbox.

ACCESS: needs a Proof account. Authenticate this client (Claude Code: /mcp → Authenticate), then call this tool again. start_login does NOT open this tool.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum wait time in seconds (default: 50, max: 600). Keep it under your MCP client's request timeout (the SDK default is 60 s) — a longer wait is cut off by the client while the server is still polling. On timeout the tool answers status "pending"; call it again with the same identifier.

name: wait_for_2fa

action_type.description: The action the session was started for: one of `TwoFAActionType` for sessions started through this API; admin-console sessions carry internal values.

grant_expires_at.description: When the grant this step-up stored stops being accepted

grant_single_use.description: Whether the grant is spent by the first act it allows

last_status.description: On timeout: the last non-terminal status observed, or null when none was

message.description: On timeout: what to do next (call the tool again with the same identifier)

status.description: "pending" when the wait ran out before a terminal state; otherwise the resource's own status

timeout_seconds.description: On timeout: the wait budget this call was given
